summary: Microbatch saturation causing ephemeral GPU starvation and queue pulses for dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Customers on a dedicated GPU pool (LexiDocs Inc.) are seeing periodic throughput collapses and p95/p99 latency spikes coinciding with short-lived high-concurrency bursts of tiny microbatches (<=8 tokens). Impact: Multiple end-to-end requests for LexiDocs indexing and chat features failed to meet latency SLOs; observed client retries and increased token cost due to repeated partial responses. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved) in us-west-2, production, mixed model routing pinned to redwood/rwkv-7b and open/gpt-13b-quant. Observed behavior: - Repeated pulses of queued requests lasting 20-90s producing p99 latency spikes from baseline ~120ms to ~1.1-1.4s. - Aggregate throughput drops by ~40-55% during pulses. - GPU attach/allocate churn: GPUs appear briefly under-utilized (5-10%) then rapidly pinned (90%+) as many tiny worklets hammer the scheduler. - Autoscaler does not add capacity because burst windows are shorter than scale-up cooldown and allocation heuristics consider bursts ephemeral. Expected behavior: Stable throughput with gradual autoscaler scale-up for sustained increases in demand, and fairness across tenants preventing a small-connection flood from causing global queue serialization. Temporary workaround attempted: Apply per-tenant connection throttling at the ingress and enable microbatch coalescing in the serving runtime for the customer's routes. Workaround reduced severity but did not fully eliminate pulses.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run a synthetic client that opens 600 concurrent short-lived streams targeting a single dedicated tenant route with requests that produce <=8 token outputs. 2) Send bursts of 100 requests every 200ms for 60 seconds. 3) Observe queue length, scheduler latency, and GPU allocation metrics via the dedicated pool dashboard. 4) Repeat with microbatching disabled and enabled to compare behavior.

investigation_notes: Observed high churn in allocation traces: lots of short attach/detach calls that coincide with request bursts.
Kernel-level GPU utilization shows oscillation (5% -> 95%) on affected nodes, indicating many tiny kernels launched frequently instead of sustained occupancy.
Autoscaler logs show bursts below configured scale-up window (default 60s) and the predictive sensor filters them out as noise.

Hypothesis: small/short-lived streams from LexiDocs (fanout-indexer microtasks) cause scheduler serialization and prevent efficient batching; noisy neighbor behavior results when many concurrent tiny streams from one tenant hold slots briefly and block larger batched work.
Checked RBAC and tenant-routing: no recent config changes. No GPU driver crashes found in the timeframe.
Related PR in runtime (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8271) contains a microbatch coalescing improvement but is not deployed to this pool.
Heap of KV-cache metadata for the customer's routes showed rapid churn but not sustained growth (so not a cache pressure issue).
Authored a small load harness to reproduce locally against staging dedicated nodes; reproduction succeeded when using many short streams with default coalescing disabled.
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Collected customer traces and initial dashboard screenshots; marked as P1 due to SLA risk.
Rafael Ortega (SRE): Confirmed churn in allocation; requested full allocation traces and node-level GPU utilization profiles.
LexiDocs (Customer): Reported intermittent 502s and saw client-side retries spike during the pulses; asking for ETA on root cause.
Rafael Ortega (SRE): Deployed temporary ingress rate-limiter rule targeting LexiDocs routes to smooth microburst fanout; asked if customer can stagger index workers as well.
Maya Chen (Support): Customer tested with reduced concurrency; pulses decreased in magnitude but not eliminated.
resolution: Mitigation applied: enabled microbatch coalescing flag for the customer's route and added a conservative per-tenant connection cap at the ingress (worker-level). This reduced the p99 latency spikes from ~1.3s to ~260ms and restored ~80% of lost throughput. Autoscaler tuning: lowered scale-up detection window from 60s to 25s for the affected dedicated pool to be more responsive to recurrent short bursts. Rollout notes: microbatch coalescing enabled via runtime flag rolled to pool-dedicated-37 on 2026-03-14 14:10 UTC; ingress throttling rule deployed 2026-03-14 14:05 UTC. No code changes required for immediate mitigation.
follow_up_actions: Create a targeted autoscaler policy for dedicated pools that balances responsiveness to short recurring bursts against oscillation risk (owner: SRE).
Merge and canary the microbatch coalescing PR (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8271) into the next runtime release and monitor kernel occupancy (owner: runtime team).
Add an observability panel to surface ephemeral-attach counts and average microbatch size per-tenant over rolling 1m windows (owner: Observability).
Customer-facing recommendation: advise LexiDocs to batch index work into slightly larger payloads or add jitter to stagger worker start times for long-running migrations (owner: CSE).
